mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 6.0% over a 3-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings weakness and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 6.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity, which precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines in a late-cycle expansion regime, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1000 thousand units over a 3-month period signals reduced consumer confidence and weaker economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 1000, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a policy response to rising inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to uncertainty.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS falls, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 over a 3-month period signals manufacturing contraction, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
